steps.text: Some changes can be undone (reversible), others can't (irreversible). Let's sort a few.
Look at each change and decide: can it be reversed? Melting ice can — freeze it back. Then check your answer.
Burning paper cannot be reversed — the ash can't become paper again. That's irreversible.
Rule of thumb: physical changes are usually reversible; chemical changes are usually irreversible.

coach.mission: Sort each change into reversible or irreversible.
whenStuck: Ask: can I get the original substance back?
If yes, it's reversible; if not, it's irreversible.
whenWrong: Melting and freezing can be undone — reversible. Burning cannot — irreversible.
New substance formed usually means irreversible.
whenCorrect: Right — you can undo that one, so it's reversible.
Right — that change can't be undone, so it's irreversible.
coach.done: You've sorted reversible and irreversible changes. Try more, or move on when you're ready.
